tour.designDesc: From blank canvas to a print-ready PDF: templates, backgrounds, the editor, and export.
tour.dl1Body: These are real Avery products with print-verified measurements. Pick by shape and size — no pixels, no coordinates, no math.
tour.dl2Body: The label pulls its product name, ingredient list and warnings from the recipe you pick here, so back labels write themselves.
tour.dl3Body: Use your own photos, free stock search, or the AI tab. AI images sometimes invent borders at the edges — the editor’s dimmed ring shows exactly what gets trimmed so nothing important is lost.
tour.dl4Body: Every design starts with the same four layers: white base, background, a soft legibility overlay, and your text & logo on top. The pink line is the cut; keep important things inside the dashed safe zone.
tour.dl5Body: Text, shapes, your photos and logo, QR codes and auto-layouts all live in this rail. Everything you add snaps to center with magenta guide lines.
tour.dl6Body: This floating window is draggable — move it wherever you like. The Layers tab reorders by drag-and-drop, and Ctrl-click selects several layers to group them.
tour.dl7Body: Export places your label onto the exact Avery grid as a true PDF — never the browser print dialog. Print it at 100% scale and the stickers line up with the die-cuts.
tour.fi1Body: Every supplier receipt goes here — vendor, date, line items, tax. There’s a CSV export when the accountant asks.
tour.fi2Body: Link a receipt line to an ingredient or material and tick “sync” — the new price flows straight into Inventory, so costs never go stale.
tour.fi3Body: Sales from completed Orders minus everything you spent = real profit, by month. Green bars are sales, red are spending.
tour.financesDesc: Expense receipts, price syncing, and the profit picture.
tour.gettingStartedDesc: A quick lap around the whole app — five minutes, no reading required afterwards.
tour.gs1Body: Everything lives in this one app: design print-ready labels, keep recipes and ingredient prices, track client orders, and watch your profit. Nothing is uploaded — it all stays on this computer.
tour.gs2Body: These tabs are the app’s rooms: Workspace (saved designs), Recipes, Ingredients, Inventory (prices & stock), Orders (client sales) and Finances (spending & profit).
tour.gs3Body: This button begins the guided label flow: pick a real Avery shape, choose a recipe, pick a background, refine the design, then print. The app does all the math.
tour.gs4Body: Wherever you are in the flow, this bar shows the step you’re on. Click any step to jump ahead — nothing is ever locked away.
tour.gs5Body: Tap any ingredient and answer two questions — what did you pay, what size was it. The app turns that into cost per gram or drop, and every recipe then knows its exact material cost.
tour.gs6Body: When a client buys, log it here. Marking the order Completed deducts the exact ingredients from stock and saves a PDF receipt for the client — automatically.
tour.gs7Body: Log purchase receipts here (they can update Inventory prices as you type). With Orders on one side and receipts on the other, the profit panel shows what you actually earned.
tour.gs8Body: That’s the lap! Replay this or any deeper tour from the ? button in the header, any time. Tips around the app can be snoozed with ✕ or turned off with “Got it”.
tour.inv1Body: Tap any card and enter what you paid and the container size. Cost per gram (or per drop for oils) calculates itself — that’s the whole job.
tour.inv2Body: Quick Set gives every ingredient in a category one baseline price — perfect for a 36-color mica set. Fine-tune individual ingredients later.
tour.inv2Title: Price a whole category at once
tour.inv3Body: Inside the price window you can paste the shop page you bought from — the app reads the price and size for you (the built-in offline AI helps on messy pages) and remembers the link for reordering.
tour.inv4Body: Enter how much of an ingredient you have on hand and completed Orders subtract usage automatically. Leave it empty to skip tracking — it’s always optional.
tour.inv5Body: Anything out or running low appears here, with a Buy button that opens the saved supplier page and a Restocked button that refills the count.
tour.inventoryDesc: Zero-math ingredient costs, bulk pricing, supplier links, and stock tracking.
tour.or1Body: Type the client’s name (returning clients auto-suggest), pick the soaps and quantities — prices pre-fill from each recipe’s retail price.
tour.or2Body: Marking an order Completed shows exactly which grams and drops will leave your stock, then saves a professional PDF receipt for the client. Reopen undoes the deduction precisely.
tour.or3Body: “Print labels” queues the saved designs for the ordered soaps onto one ink-saving sheet, with quantities already filled in.
tour.or4Body: “Repeat” starts a fresh order with the same client and items. The client filter above the list shows anyone’s full history and lifetime total.
tour.ordersDesc: Client sales, automatic stock deduction, PDF receipts, and printing the right labels.
tour.pr1Body: A tiny batch code (pre-filled from today’s date) prints inside the bottom edge of every label — so you always know which batch and cure date a bar came from. Clear the box to skip it.
tour.pr2Body: Select several saved designs and print them together on a single Avery sheet — a part-used sheet of sticker paper never goes to waste.
tour.pr3Body: If stickers come out shifted, print the calibration page and measure the 1-inch square. If it isn’t exactly 1 inch, the printer is scaling — set it to 100% / Actual size.
tour.pr4Body: The golden rule: in the print dialog choose “Actual size”, never “Fit to page”. The PDFs are dimension-exact — any scaling breaks the alignment.
tour.printingDesc: Lot codes, batch sheets that waste nothing, and fixing misaligned printers.
